newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin orders full government reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin orders full government reshuffle.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday ordered a full reorganisation of the Russian government, leaving only Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and a first deputy premier in place, Interfax news agency said.

"Only the prime minister and the first deputy prime minister will stay, all other members of the cabinet resign. The bulk of the new government will be formed within one week," Interfax said. It did not give the first deputy prime minister's name but it was clear that Anatoly Chubais, appointed only last Friday, would remain in his new post.
The Kremlin press service could not immediately confirm the Interfax report, saying only that it was preparing a formal statement to be issued shortly.

Yeltsin said last Thursday he would reorganise the government, bringing in new "competent and energetic" people. The next day he appointed his loyal ally, liberal Anatoly Chubais, to the post of first deputy prime minister.
Kremlin sources and Russian media reports said Chernomyrdin and Chubais would be given a free hand in forming a more streamlined and efficient government.
